summary: Elevated TTFB for chat completions after serving-runtime upgrade (models: redwood-rlhf-13b-v2)
description:
Issue summary: Customer (GrooveAI) reports an increase in TTFB (time-to-first-token) for chat completions after the 2026-02-19 serving-runtime upgrade. Impact: End users see long initial response delays (UI spinner >2s), some clients hit client-side 3s timeouts and reconnect, resulting in duplicate completions and poor UX. Environment: Production (us-east), traffic routed to dedicated pool for enterprise customers. Observed starting ~2026-02-19 22:30 UTC after rollout of serving-runtime v4.12.2.

Observed behavior: Subsequent tokens stream at expected rate once first token is emitted; overall token throughput unchanged. The regression manifests as increased p50/p95 TTFB only.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Using customer's API key or repro account, send a chat completion request to v1/chat/completions with model=redwood-rlhf-13b-v2 and short prompt (~30 tokens).

2) Example curl: curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer <KEY>" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"redwood-rlhf-13b-v2","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Write a single-sentence product description"}] }'
3) Observe time to first byte/token in response (measure TTFB). Repeat across multiple requests and compare to baseline (pre-upgrade).
4) Reproduce tends to be more consistent when request arrives after a model has been idle for >60s (cold interval).

metrics_summary: Baseline p95 TTFB for redwood-rlhf-13b-v2 (pre-upgrade): ~120ms. Post-upgrade observed p95 TTFB: ~900ms - 1200ms for first token. Subsequent token latencies unchanged. Increased CPU sys time observed on scheduler and higher kernel compile counts per minute.
investigation_notes: 2026-02-20 - Initial triage by Support (Maya): Confirmed customer-side reproducible; collected traces and sample request IDs.
2026-02-20 - Eng (Liam): Looked at traces in tracing service (trace-8f7a). Noted long attention kernel compile step (~800ms) on first request for some model configurations.
Hypothesis A: New kernel selection/compilation path in v4.12.2 triggers JIT/kernel compile on first request for some quantized models leading to elevated TTFB.
Hypothesis B: KV cache warming was made lazy by change in cache policy; cold requests pay cost for warming (we see KVCache miss logs).
Telemetry: Increased 'kernel_compile' metric and 'kv_cache_miss' spike starting at 2026-02-19 22:20 UTC coincident with rollout window.
Observed that requests pinned to older runtime (v4.11.9) do not show regression - points to runtime change rather than model artifact.
Loaded flamegraph for a slow request: ~60% time spent in kernel compile and serialization; disk IO not a major factor.
comments: 2026-02-20 - Maya Patel (Support): Reached out to customer to request sample request IDs and confirm affected model versions. Customer supplied request ids: cust-req-004, cust-req-018.
2026-02-20 - Liam Chen (SRE): Correlated traces; opened internal bug INT-4021 for kernel compile regression and added to this ticket as linked issue.

2026-02-21 - Engineering (R&D): Reproduced locally with docker image runtime:v4.12.2; confirmed compile time ~750-900ms for first request on redwood-quant-13b-8bit. Created PR to gate compilation behind async precompile flag.
2026-02-22 - Customer (GrooveAI): Noted partial improvement when pinning to model version redwood-rlhf-13b-v1 but still sees occasional spikes; asked for ETA on fix.
2026-02-23 - Liam Chen: Deployed hotfix v4.12.3 to a subset of nodes (canary) which disables on-demand kernel compile for quantized paths; observing TTFB returning to baseline on canary nodes.
root_cause_summary: A change in serving-runtime v4.12.2 introduced an on-demand kernel compilation path for certain quantized models. The compile occurs on the first request after idle, adding ~700-900ms to TTFB. Additionally, cache warming was deferred in this release for some sessions, compounding initial-request overhead.
workaround: 1) Pin affected workloads to redwood-rlhf-13b-v1 (previous model variant) or route to nodes still on runtime v4.11.9. 2) For customers on Dedicated, add a short keep-alive traffic to prevent cold intervals. 3) If using our SDK, enable 'prewarm_kv_cache' flag (temporary config) to reduce cache miss impact.
resolution: Hotfix v4.12.3 rolled to canary pool 2026-02-23 which disables on-demand kernel compile and restores previous compile-on-deploy behavior. Early canary metrics show p95 TTFB back to ~140ms. Plan: Gradual rollout to all prod pools over 2026-02-24 pending monitoring. Customer notified and offered option to pin to older runtime until full rollout completes.
follow_up_tasks: INT-4021 - Fix kernel compile path (engineering) - in progress (see linked PRs)
Add automated regression test for TTFB on model idle->first-request transition
Update runbook to include prewarm_kv_cache config and guidance for upgrade windows
notes: Customer-facing support ticket. Keep GrooveAI CSM (Anika Rao) in copy for major updates. Priority elevated due to enterprise SLA impact.
